question: Why did late deliveries jump to 19% for orders placed in March 2018?

sources.what_it_holds: Order management system: customers and orders with status, purchase/approval timestamps, carrier handoff, customer delivery, and promised delivery dates
sources.grain: oms.customers: one row per customer; oms.orders: one row per order

sources.what_it_holds: Seller platform: order items (one row per item with seller, product, shipping deadline, price, freight), seller master data, and product catalog with Portuguese/English categories and dimensions
sources.grain: sellers.order_items: one row per order item; sellers.sellers: one row per seller; sellers.products: one row per product

sources.what_it_holds: Payment gateway: order payments with type, installments, sequential number, and value
sources.grain: payments.order_payments: one row per payment installment (an order can have multiple rows)

sources.what_it_holds: Review platform: customer reviews with score 1-5, comment text in Portuguese, and creation/answer timestamps
sources.grain: feedback.reviews: one row per review (one per order)

sources.what_it_holds: External events: verified strikes, peak seasons, and disruptions with start/end dates, region, confidence, and sources
Documents: news briefs on external events with body, sender, recipients, and sent date

joins.meaning: link an order to the customer who placed it
seller who fulfilled an order item
product details for an order item

date_columns.meaning: when the customer placed the order
when the order was handed to the carrier
when the customer received the order
delivery date promised to the customer (date only, no time)
deadline for the seller to hand the item to the carrier
when the review was created (stored as string)
when the review was answered (stored as string)
start date of the external event (stored as string)
end date of the external event (stored as string)
when the news brief was sent (stored as string)

status_values.meaning: geographic scope of the external event

caveats: LATE definition: delivered on a later calendar date than promised — CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS DATE) > CAST(order_estimated_delivery_date AS DATE); do not compare raw timestamps because promised date has no time of day and same-day deliveries would be wrongly flagged
oms.orders.order_estimated_delivery_date is a timestamp with midnight time; cast to DATE before comparing
feedback.reviews.review_creation_date and review_answer_timestamp are stored as strings and need casting to timestamp/date
signals.events.start_date and end_date are stored as strings and need casting to date
docs.documents.sent_at is stored as a string and needs casting to timestamp
payments.order_payments is at payment-installment grain — one order can have multiple rows (payment_sequential), so joining without aggregation can duplicate order-level measures
sellers.order_items is at order-item grain — one order can have multiple items, so joining to orders without aggregation multiplies order rows
oms.orders contains non-delivered statuses (canceled, unavailable, processing, etc.) where delivery/promised dates may be NULL — filter to delivered orders before computing lateness
customer_city and customer_state are lowercase strings; normalize before comparing with external region values

findings.statement: Measure the symptom: late deliveries for orders placed March 2018, against a normal baseline
findings.claim: 1,328 of 7,003 delivered orders placed March 2018 were late (19.0%), against 5.6% for a normal baseline: months 2017-09, 2017-10, 2017-12, 2018-01 (left out as abnormal: 2017-11, 2018-02): a difference of 13.4 points (confidence interval 12.4 to 14.4).

fixed.reason: Measured directly by the analysis engine.

findings.statement: What the late orders are worth, and how their customers rated them
findings.claim: The 1,328 late orders were worth R$ 187,138 (order value), with R$ 35,034 of freight paid on them. Their customers gave them 2.1 stars on average, against 4.2 for the orders that arrived on time; 68.3% of their reviews were 1 or 2 stars, against 10.7%.

fixed.reason: Measured directly by the analysis engine: the value at stake, not what a fix would cost.

findings.statement: Sellers handed orders to the carrier later than normal
findings.claim: Hand-over to the carrier (seller or warehouse): typically 2.0 days, the same as at baseline; four in five orders within 5.0 days, the same as at baseline. This stage moved the other way (share of the 13.4-point rise, from 5.6% to 19.0% late: -1.6%).

fixed.reason: Went the other way (share of the rise: -1.6%).

findings.claim: Carrier transit: typically 10.0 days against 8.0 at baseline; four in five orders within 21.0 days against 15.0 at baseline. Had this stage stayed as it was at baseline, 72.7% of the 13.4-point rise (from 5.6% to 19.0% late) would not have happened.

Promised delivery window: typically 22.0 days against 25.0 at baseline; four in five orders within 28.0 days against 31.0 at baseline. Had this stage stayed as it was at baseline, 26.7% of the 13.4-point rise (from 5.6% to 19.0% late) would not have happened.

findings.statement: The rise is concentrated in some places (by customer state)
findings.claim: Where the rise sits, by customer state: SP: 20.1% of the rise from 42.4% of the orders (3.2% -> 9.4% late); RJ: 18.9% of the rise from 12.3% of the orders (12.8% -> 34.5% late); MG: 16.6% of the rise from 12.2% of the orders (2.3% -> 20.4% late).

fixed.reason: Concentrated in RJ (share of the rise at least 1.5x share of orders). This says where, not why.

findings.statement: The rise is concentrated in some segments (by seller state)
findings.claim: Where the rise sits, by seller state: SP: 81.5% of the rise from 73.5% of the orders (5.8% -> 20.5% late); RJ: 8.0% of the rise from 4.2% of the orders (6.1% -> 31.7% late); PR: 4.6% of the rise from 8.3% of the orders (4.3% -> 11.3% late).

fixed.reason: Spread broadly: no segment's share of the rise is well above its share of orders.

findings.statement: A surge in orders overloaded hand-over or transit
findings.claim: 225.9 orders per day vs 234.1 in the four weeks before (0.96x); mean hand-over 3.3 vs 3.5 days, mean transit 13.0 vs 13.4 days.

fixed.reason: Volume did not rise enough, or the chain did not slow with it.

findings.statement: The symptom is a data artefact (missing or impossible dates, duplicates, definition)
findings.claim: 0 delivered orders have a missing date and 0 an impossible date order, out of 7,211 in scope; 208 not-delivered orders are left out. Late is 19.0% comparing calendar dates and 21.4% comparing raw timestamps (WhyChain uses calendar dates: the promise has no time of day).

fixed.reason: Anomalies are 0.0% of orders: too few to explain the rise.

findings.claim: Review mentions per thousand orders (focus vs reference): delay 14.7 vs 4.1; strike 0.9 vs 0.8; not received 50.3 vs 22.8; post office 16.0 vs 11.8.

findings.statement: Carnival holiday 2018 (2018-02-12 to 2018-02-14, Brazil) delayed deliveries
findings.claim: Carnival holiday 2018 (2018-02-12 to 2018-02-14): carrier transit was 11.1 days just before it, against a normal 8.7; with the event, transit moved 0.6 days and the late rate 0.3 points against the prior trend.

fixed.reason: The effect was already there before the event.

findings.statement: Severe storm in Rio de Janeiro city (2018-02-15 to 2018-02-15, RJ) delayed deliveries
findings.claim: Severe storm in Rio de Janeiro city (2018-02-15 to 2018-02-15): carrier transit was 11.1 days just before it, against a normal 8.7; with the event, transit moved 0.6 days and the late rate 0.3 points against the prior trend. Larger in RJ than elsewhere: no.

fixed.reason: The effect was already there before the event.

findings.statement: Correios workers' national strike over health plan (Mar 2018) (2018-03-12 to 2018-03-13, Brazil) delayed deliveries
findings.claim: Correios workers' national strike over health plan (Mar 2018) (2018-03-12 to 2018-03-13): carrier transit was 14.1 days just before it, against a normal 8.7; with the event, transit moved -0.5 days and the late rate 0.0 points against the prior trend.

fixed.reason: The effect was already there before the event.

findings.statement: What the written record (news briefs, contracts, email) says about the period, places and events in question
findings.claim: The written record reports three events overlapping March 2018: (1) Federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro public security, decreed 16 Feb 2018 and running until 31 Dec 2018, limited to public security with Army General Braga Netto in command; (2) Correios R$3 emergency surcharge on parcels to Rio city and metro area, announced 27 Feb 2018, due from 6 Mar 2018, suspended by a Procon-RJ injunction in March then reinstated by TRF2 appeals court in April, ended 16 Nov 2018; (3) Correios workers' national strike over health-plan changes, begun 12 Mar 2018, called off 13 Mar with return to work 14 Mar, though Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo unions still had assemblies pending. The documents describe who, what, where, and when for each event but do not establish any causal link to the late delivery
findings.who_knew: operations inbox (recipients of all three news briefs)

T1.A1.title: Late deliveries: focus vs reference

summary.reference: a normal baseline: months 2017-09, 2017-10, 2017-12, 2018-01 (left out as abnormal: 2017-11, 2018-02)

T1.A1.method: Late = delivered on a later calendar date than promised. Focus: orders placed March 2018. Compared with a normal baseline: months 2017-09, 2017-10, 2017-12, 2018-01 (left out as abnormal: 2017-11, 2018-02). 95% Wilson intervals; the difference uses a normal approximation.
T1.A1.sql:
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status AS status,
       o.order_purchase_timestamp AS purchase_ts, o.order_delivered_carrier_date AS handover_ts,
       o.order_delivered_customer_date AS delivered_ts, o.order_estimated_delivery_date AS promised_ts,
       c.customer_state, s.seller_state, i.seller_id, p.product_category_name_english AS category,
       i.n_items, i.price, i.freight
FROM oms.orders o
JOIN oms.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, MIN(seller_id) AS seller_id, MIN(product_id) AS product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_items,
                  SUM(price) AS price, SUM(freight_value) AS freight
           FROM sellers.order_items GROUP BY order_id) i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN sellers.sellers s ON s.seller_id = i.seller_id
LEFT JOIN sellers.products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id

T2.A1.title: What the late orders are worth
T2.A1.method: The focus orders, split into late and on time: their number, order value (the sum of item prices) and freight paid, and the stars their customers gave in reviews (an order with several reviews counts their mean). This is the value at stake, not the cost of fixing it, which the data doesn't hold.

T3.A1.title: Which delivery stage explains the rise
rows: hand-over to the carrier (seller or warehouse)

summary.reference: a normal baseline: months 2017-09, 2017-10, 2017-12, 2018-01 (left out as abnormal: 2017-11, 2018-02)

T3.A1.method: For each stage, every focus order's days are replaced by the reference value at the same rank (within the same customer_state) and the late rate is recomputed. Exact Shapley values over the three stages split the rise so the contributions add up; 'other' is what no stage explains. rows: Federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro public security

Decree 9,288 of 16 Feb 2018 placed public security in Rio de Janeiro state under federal intervention until 31 Dec 2018, with Army General Walter Braga Netto in command of the state police and fire brigade.
Correios R$3 emergency surcharge on parcels to Rio metro area

On 27 Feb 2018 Correios announced a R$3 surcharge per parcel to Rio city and its metro area, citing extreme violence against its staff and vehicles, due from 6 Mar. A Procon-RJ injunction suspended it in March, an appeals court reinstated it in April, and Correios ended it on 16 Nov 2018.
Correios workers' national strike over health plan (Mar 2018)

Correios workers began an open-ended national strike on 12 Mar 2018 against health-plan changes. After a TST ruling the same day, the federation called it off on 13 Mar with return to work on 14 Mar; Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo unions still had assemblies pending.

       c.customer_state, s.seller_state, i.seller_id, p.product_category_name_english AS category,

FROM oms.orders o
JOIN oms.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, MIN(seller_id) AS seller_id, MIN(product_id) AS product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_items,
                  SUM(price) AS price, SUM(freight_value) AS freight
           FROM sellers.order_items GROUP BY order_id) i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN sellers.sellers s ON s.seller_id = i.seller_id
LEFT JOIN sellers.products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id

brief:
## Summary
- **What happened:** 1,328 of 7,003 delivered orders placed March 2018 were late (19.0%), against 5.6% for a normal baseline. [T1.A1] The 1,328 late orders were worth R$ 187,138 (order value), with R$ 35,034 of freight paid on them. Their customers gave them 2.1 stars on average, against 4.2 for the orders that arrived on time; 68.3% of their reviews were 1 or 2 stars, against 10.7%. [T2.A1][T2.A2]
- **Why:** Carrier transit got slower (72.7% of the rise) and promised delivery windows got shorter (26.7% of the rise). Ruled out: Carnival holiday 2018; Severe storm in Rio de Janeiro city; Correios workers' national strike over health plan.
- **What to do:** A2. Get transit back to normal in SP, RJ, MG (593 orders; R$ 83,603 of orders at stake, 415 with a 1- or 2-star review; within limits). A1. Add delivery-promise buffers where transit outruns the promise (255 orders; R$ 37,740 of orders at stake, 150 with a 1- or 2-star review; needs approval).

## Answer
Late deliveries jumped to 19.0% for March 2018 orders, up from a 5.6% baseline [T1.A1]. The rise was driven by slower carrier transit (72.7% of the increase) and shorter promised delivery windows (26.7% of the increase) [T4.A1][T5.A1].

## Root causes
1. **Carrier transit got slower** (72.7% of the rise). [T4.A1][T4.A2]
2. **Promised delivery windows got shorter** (26.7% of the rise). [T5.A1][T5.A2]

## Where it happened
- Where the rise sits, by customer state: SP: 20.1% of the rise from 42.4% of the orders (3.2% -> 9.4% late); RJ: 18.9% of the rise from 12.3% of the orders (12.8% -> 34.5% late); MG: 16.6% of the rise from 12.2% of the orders (2.3% -> 20.4% late). [T6.A1][T6.A2]
- Where the rise sits, by seller state: SP: 81.5% of the rise from 73.5% of the orders (5.8% -> 20.5% late); RJ: 8.0% of the rise from 4.2% of the orders (6.1% -> 31.7% late); PR: 4.6% of the rise from 8.3% of the orders (4.3% -> 11.3% late). [T7.A1][T7.A2]

## Ruled out
- **Sellers handed orders to the carrier later than normal**: Went the other way (share of the rise: -1.6%). [T3.A1][T3.A2]
- **A surge in orders overloaded hand-over or transit**: Volume did not rise enough, or the chain did not slow with it. [T8.A1][T8.A2]
- **The symptom is a data artefact (missing or impossible dates, duplicates, definition)**: Anomalies are 0.0% of orders: too few to explain the rise. [T9.A1][T9.A2]
- **Carnival holiday 2018 (2018-02-12 to 2018-02-14, Brazil) delayed deliveries**: The effect was already there before the event. [T11.A1][T11.A2]
- **Severe storm in Rio de Janeiro city (2018-02-15 to 2018-02-15, RJ) delayed deliveries**: The effect was already there before the event. [T12.A1][T12.A2]
- **Correios workers' national strike over health plan (Mar 2018) (2018-03-12 to 2018-03-13, Brazil) delayed deliveries**: The effect was already there before the event. [T13.A1][T13.A2]

## What customers and the written record say
- Review mentions per thousand orders (focus vs reference): delay 14.7 vs 4.1; strike 0.9 vs 0.8; not received 50.3 vs 22.8; post office 16.0 vs 11.8. [T10.A1][T10.A2]
- Federal intervention in Rio de Janeiro (2018-02-16): "On 16 February 2018 President Michel Temer signed Decree 9,288, placing public security in Rio de Janeiro state under federal intervention until 31 December 2018." [T14.D1]
- Correios surcharge on Rio-bound parcels (2018-02-27): "On 27 February 2018 Correios announced a R$3 emergency surcharge per parcel delivered to Rio de Janeiro city and its metropolitan region, citing extreme levels of violence and the cost of protecting staff, parcels and units." [T14.D2]
- Correios strike, March 2018 (2018-03-12): "Correios workers began an open-ended national strike on Monday 12 March 2018 (from 22:00 on 11 March for night shifts). They opposed health-plan changes that introduced monthly fees and removed dependants, as well as outsourcing and privatization." [T14.D3]

## Recommended actions
| Action | Protects | Value at stake | Est. cost | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1. Add delivery-promise buffers where transit outruns the promise: RJ +9 days, BA +6 days, MG +2 days, CE +14 days, ES +8 days [A.A1] | 255 orders | R$ 37,740 (150 left a 1- or 2-star review) | not computed (no cost data) | needs approval: changes what customers are promised |
| A2. Get transit back to normal in SP, RJ, MG: 593 late orders would have arrived on time [A.A3][T4.A1] | 593 orders | R$ 83,603 (415 left a 1- or 2-star review) | not computed (no cost data) | within limits |

## How we know
- **Carrier transit got slower** (72.7% of the rise): Carrier transit: typically 10.0 days against 8.0 at baseline; four in five orders within 21.0 days against 15.0 at baseline. Had this stage stayed as it was at baseline, 72.7% of the 13.4-point rise (from 5.6% to 19.0% late) would not have happened. [T4.A1][T4.A2]
- **Promised delivery windows got shorter** (26.7% of the rise): Promised delivery window: typically 22.0 days against 25.0 at baseline; four in five orders within 28.0 days against 31.0 at baseline. Had this stage stayed as it was at baseline, 26.7% of the 13.4-point rise (from 5.6% to 19.0% late) would not have happened. [T5.A1][T5.A2]
- **What the late orders are worth, and how their customers rated them**: The 1,328 late orders were worth R$ 187,138 (order value), with R$ 35,034 of freight paid on them. Their customers gave them 2.1 stars on average, against 4.2 for the orders that arrived on time; 68.3% of their reviews were 1 or 2 stars, against 10.7%. [T2.A1][T2.A2]
- The confirmed stages (72.7% and 26.7%) together explain 99.4% of the measured rise; the rest is mix and interactions.
- Every number above was computed by the analysis engine from the cited results, and checked against their cells. Verdicts follow fixed rules (see the README), not a model's judgement.

## Ask why next
- Why were deliveries to Rio de Janeiro late for orders placed March 2018? (The rise is concentrated in Rio de Janeiro: what made it worse there?)
headline: 1,328 of 7,003 delivered orders placed March 2018 were late (19.0%), against 5.6% for a normal baseline. Main causes: carrier transit got slower (72.7% of the rise) and promised delivery windows got shorter (26.7% of the rise).
